name: hydra
highlights: -I — ignore an existing restore file (don't wait 10 seconds)
-s — if the service is on a different default port, define it here
-p — or -P FILE try password PASS, or load several passwords from FILE
-y — disable use of symbols in bruteforce, see above
-r — use a non-random shuffling method for option -x
-u — loop around users, not passwords (effective! implied with -x)

flags.name: -R
flags.description: restore a previous aborted/crashed session

flags.name: -I
flags.description: ignore an existing restore file (don't wait 10 seconds)

flags.name: -S
flags.description: perform an SSL connect

flags.name: -s
flags.description: if the service is on a different default port, define it here

flags.name: -p
flags.description: or -P FILE try password PASS, or load several passwords from FILE

flags.name: -y
flags.description: disable use of symbols in bruteforce, see above

flags.name: -r
flags.description: use a non-random shuffling method for option -x

flags.name: -u
flags.description: loop around users, not passwords (effective! implied with -x)

flags.name: -C
flags.description: colon separated "login:pass" format, instead of -L/-P options

flags.name: -M
flags.description: list of servers to attack, one entry per line, ':' to specify port

flags.name: -o
flags.description: write found login/password pairs to FILE instead of stdout

flags.name: -f
flags.description: exit when a login/pass pair is found (-M: -f per host, -F global)

flags.name: -t
flags.description: run TASKS number of connects in parallel per target (default: 16)

flags.name: -T
flags.description: run TASKS connects in parallel overall (for -M, default: 64)

flags.name: -w
flags.description: wait time for a response (32) / between connects per thread (0)

flags.name: -c
flags.description: wait time per login attempt over all threads (enforces -t 1)
use IPv4 (default) / IPv6 addresses (put always in [] also in -M)

flags.name: -v
flags.description: verbose mode / show login+pass for each attempt / debug mode

flags.name: -O
flags.description: use old SSL v2 and v3

flags.name: -K
flags.description: do not redo failed attempts (good for -M mass scanning)

flags.name: -q
flags.description: do not print messages about connection errors

flags.name: -U
flags.description: service module usage details

flags.name: -m
flags.description: options specific for a module, see -U output for information

flags.name: -h
flags.description: more command line options (COMPLETE HELP)

examples.explanation: Guess IMAP credentials on a range of hosts using a list of colon-separated username/password pairs
